name: Automations
summary: A menu page for saved schedules: a list of automations (report recipes and blueprint launches) with next fire and last run, an inline editor with a live cron preview, run history that names why a run was skipped, and the Scrooge report with a fix-it button per finding.
description: An automation is a cron schedule on this computer's clock plus one thing to do, today a report recipe (Scrooge). The Automations page lists them with their next fire time, newest run and an on or off switch; edit, run now and delete sit on each row. Cron also reads the third Tuesday style, written 2#3 in the day-of-week field, and POST /automations/schedule/parse turns a sentence like every third Tuesday at 5 PM into a cron through the connected AI, for confirmation only. The editor checks the cron as you type and shows the next five fires or the reason it is refused (two fires under 15 minutes apart, or never). Under the selected automation, run history shows each run's status, cost and named reason; consecutive skips with the same reason fold into one row that gives the count and dates. A run with a report opens it in place: totals, projects, lever coverage including the levers that could not be measured, and the findings. Every action is an authenticated route, and the page follows the automations and automation_runs push topics instead of polling. A cron agent target runs the installed claude (claude -p) on a schedule in a project folder under a picked login: read only by default, file edits inside the folder as an opt-in, or no permission prompts only after typing a confirming phrase in the app (never settable over MCP), with a spend cap, turn limit and time limit on every run. A finished agent run shows its final text and a continue in a session button that opens a Carnivore session resuming its conversation. The page has three tabs: automations (the list), sessions (projects, the sessions under each, and the automations on each node, with unassigned for the rest, each node showing its next run and last result) and, while the task manager addon is enabled, task manager (the task manager items that carry a schedule, by list, read only). Schedule this on a session or project in the drawer opens the editor already pointed at it. A scheduler pause switch on the page (and in the menu bar tray menu, which also lists the next three runs and the last three results and opens this page) holds every scheduled run as a skipped run with the reason scheduler_paused; run now still works. The page opens simple: an automations tab of tiles and cards, a sessions tab that is a review feed with a quick-view drawer, and an advanced tab that keeps everything above (table, pane, run feed, counters, scheduler log, commands, pause switch) unchanged. A run title and summary are written by code on the server, never by an AI.
surfaces: automations sessions tab (the run feed and reader)
drawer session row menu: schedule this
where: The drawer's menu tab: the automations row under blueprints, hotkey u while the menu has focus. Deep link #automations; a run's report is #automations/run/<run id>.
A notification's link for an automation report opens the page on that run.

The tabs under the page title: automations (tiles and cards), sessions (a review feed of runs) and advanced (the table and its detail pane, the run feed with its reader, counters, scheduler log and commands). The chosen tab is remembered per device. Deep link #automations/advanced.

The drawer: a session row's menu carries schedule this (the project heading's menu dropped its entry 2026-10-19). Deep link #automations/new/session/<session uuid> or #automations/new/project/<project id>.
how_to: Open the menu tab and choose automations. The line under the title says what the page is.
Press new automation, give it a name and a cron (for example 0 7 * * 1 for Mondays at 7), pick the report to run and save. The next fires show under the cron field before you save.
Click an automation's row to open its pane and read its run history on the runs tab; a row that says skipped 3 times names the dates and the reason, such as the computer was asleep.
Open a run's report, read the findings and the levers the run could not measure, and press fix-it session on a finding to open a Claude session in that project with the fix prompt loaded.
Use the switch to turn an automation off without losing its schedule, and delete (then delete again in the confirm) to remove it.
Pick launch a blueprint as the target, choose the blueprint and which members to start. Each run starts fresh sessions marked auto; the newest three runs keep theirs.

Choose what it does: run a cron agent, pick a project, write the prompt, pick what it may do, then save. Open a finished run's report and press continue in a session to pick the conversation up by hand.
In the editor, add what it is for, a project, what to do about a missed run (run once or skip), retries and the longest a run may take.
Pick a target: a report, a system action, a message to a session, an allowed command, or two to four steps in order.
Select an automation to see its change log (who changed what, an agent by its session) and press scheduler log to read the log and set how it rotates.
Add allowed commands on this page with the allowed commands button next to scheduler log. A command target can only run a command on that list, typed exactly the same.

Open the sessions tab to read every run across all automations, newest first; filter by automation, status, trigger, computer or session, press a counter at the top to narrow to it, and walk the runs with j and k, jumping to the next change with u.
In the drawer, open a session's or a project's menu and choose schedule this; the editor opens with that session (or project) already chosen.

On the automations tab, read the four tiles, then the cards by when they run; the switch on a card turns it on or off, and a card opens a side drawer with run now, the next three runs, edit and open in advanced.
On the sessions tab, read each run as a title and one line, press looks good on the ones you checked or mark all reviewed, and open a run for its drawer; the full report is in advanced.
In the editor, set when it runs three ways: type a sentence, pick a repeat, weekdays and a time, or write a cron (the third Tuesday is 2#3 in the day-of-week field).
examples: Run the Scrooge report every Monday at 07:00 and read last week's findings from the page.
See that last night's run was skipped because the computer was asleep, with the reason in words.
Launch a saved blueprint every weekday morning, find its sessions marked auto in the sidebar, and watch each go to sleep when its turn ends.
Drop a swarm card titled 'weekly audit {date}' on a project's board every Monday, in todo or started right away.
Open the menu of a session that needs a nightly nudge, choose schedule this, type the message and a cron, and save.
Press the failed 24h counter on the sessions tab and read every run that failed since yesterday in one list.
Read each run as a plain title and one-line summary, such as 'nightly backup failed: the command exited with code 2'.
Type every third tuesday at 5 pm into the schedule field, check the read-back and the next fires, and create it.
media_exempt: The page's media are captured at the next version bump with the rest of the feature recapture.
